 J U D G M E N T

The original petition filed by the husband against the

wife before the Family Court seeking a decree of divorce,

was allowed. Challenging the same, the wife is in appeal.

For the sake of convenience the parties are referred to as

per their status in the Family Court.

2. The marriage between the parties were solemnised on

16.02.1987. Dissolution of marriage was sought under Section

10(1)(viii) of the Divorce Act, 1869. The claim was that,

the earlier original petition filed by the wife as OP

176/2012, seeking restitution of conjugal rights, was

decreed on 31.05.2013; since there has been no resumption of

cohabitation for the statutory period of two years, divorce
 Mat. Appeal No.1082 of 2017




 2025:KER:61183
 -: 2 :-



is liable to be granted under Section 10(1)(viii) of the

Divorce Act.

3. The Family Court, finding that there has been no

resumption of cohabitation even after lapse of two years

since the date of decree for restitution of conjugal rights,

granted a decree for divorce.
4. We have heard learned counsel on either side.

5. Section 10(1)(viii) of the Indian Divorce Act, 1869

reads thus :-

"10. Ground for dissolution of marriage.--(1) Any marriage solemnized,
 whether before or after the commencement of the Indian Divorce
 (Amendment) Act, 2001, may, on a petition presented to the District Court
 either by the husband or the wife, be dissolved on the ground that since
 the solemnization of the marriage, the respondent--

(viii) has failed to comply with a decree for restitution of conjugal
 rights for a period of two years or upwards after the passing of the decree
 against the respondent."

6. In terms of the section, if the respondent failed to

comply with the decree for restitution of conjugal rights

for a period of two years, then petitioner is entitled for

dissolution of marriage on such ground.

7. In the case at hand, it is the respondent who had

obtained a decree against the petitioner, for restitution of

conjugal rights. The petitioner failed to comply with the

judgment. The petitioner having suffered a decree and having

failed to comply with the same is not provided with any

right under the section, to obtain dissolution of marriage.

Therefore, the decree for divorce granted by the Family

Court cannot be sustained.

Resultantly, the appeal is allowed. The decree for

dissolution of marriage granted in OP 333/2015 will stand

set aside. The OP will stand dismissed. It is clarified that

this shall not affect the rights of the petitioner to seek

for dissolution of marriage on any other grounds available

under law.
